summary:
Visual QA, round 4. Not a pass: 3 UI blockers, all small. Nothing is broken and no screen looks wrong at first glance, but each is below the Linear, Stripe, Vercel bar.

What I did
- Built 16 fresh accounts through the real screens, one per billing state, plus a billing only person and an account on the production mode portal with no keys (port 3310).
- Took 809 screenshots at 1440, 768 and 390 in light and dark, plus 360 and 320 for the main screens. I looked at them on contact sheets and at full size where something looked off.
- Covered signup, plan picker, verify email, welcome, launcher, every billing tab in every state, test checkout (works, declined, bank approval), invoices, cancel and pause, seat and warehouse limits, the banners and lock screens in CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse, view only dialogs, the pricing page and the get started wizard, and the email templates.
- The portal dev server was stopped once by the system for lack of memory during my run. I started it again with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0. All 7 services are up. I changed no product code.

Round 3 visual blockers: all fixed
- Verify email no longer starts a line with a stray period.
- View only WMS dashboard: 0 hydration errors in 6 loads, and 0 of 6 on the four other pages I tried.
- Warehouse limit offer is a calm dialog now.
- One sentence for the empty invoices state, and the billing team email wraps on phones.
- The WMS banner showed "trial ended" 4 seconds after the trial ended.

Other reviewers' round 3 UI points that I could see on screen also look fixed
- Billing only person: each app shows "You have billing access only" with "Back to Billing", and the menu says "Billing only".
- The sign in side panel no longer sells a trial, and the invite panel says who you join and your role.
- The picker and the confirm dialog warn when the bundle discount ends.
- The password meter no longer shows ticks that are not true.
- Remove asks first, and "Sam is already on your team" is in our words.

Clean checks
- No sideways scroll from 320 to 1440 on about 40 pages.
- No text contrast failure on 20 pages in both themes.
- A visible focus ring on every control I tabbed to.
- Reduced motion drops the confetti.
- Buttons show a busy state within 150 ms and cannot be sent twice.
- 0 console errors on portal pages.
- At 360 by 740 the signup form shows "Create account" on the first screen, with a cart too.
- Billing off in production mode is calm and honest.

Not seen
- Real Stripe checkout and the Billing Portal (no keys).
- Google and Microsoft buttons (no client keys).
- Loading skeletons: my slow network test delayed the request itself, so it only proves the pressed tab highlights at once.

Screenshots and scripts are in /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/visual4/ (shots, sheets, scripts, notes.txt).

blockers.title: Signup password area: the code link splits the error from its field
blockers.detail:
Wrong: on /signup the bold link "Email me a code instead" sits between the password meter and rules and the password error.
- After a failed submit the order is: red field, hint, four red rules, a bold black "Email me a code instead", then the red "Enter a password." The error no longer reads as part of the field.
- The link is bold dark text with no underline, so it reads as a label. Its 48 px focus ring cuts through the "A number" and "A symbol" row above it.
- A password built on the company name (company "Harbor Supply Co", password "Harbor-Lantern-77-quiet!") shows "Too weak" and "That one is too easy to guess. Try a few words that do not go together." The words are already ones that do not go together, so the person cannot tell what to fix. The email name case does give its reason ("Do not use your email name in your password.").

Reproduce: open http://localhost:3300/signup and press Create account with an empty password. Then tab to the link. Then type the company and a password that starts with the company name.
Screenshots in docs/billing/.review/visual4: sheets/_z1.png, sheets/_s3.png, shots/a03-signup-errors--desktop-light.png, shots/a05-signup-strong--phone-dark.png.

Great looks like:
- The error sits right under the field and its rules, with nothing between.
- The code choice is its own quiet row, below the error or under the button, styled as a link. Its focus ring touches no other text.
- The company case says why: "Do not use your company name in your password."
- The same order on /invite and /reset-password if they share the layout.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/signup/signup-form.tsx (lines 396 to 413: StrengthMeter, PasswordRules, then the signup-email-code button, all above the field error); packages/auth/src/weak-passwords.ts (EASY_TO_GUESS_MESSAGE for the company_name reason)

blockers.title: Confirm change dialog drops keyboard focus on close
blockers.detail:
Wrong: on /billing/plan with a paid plan, closing the confirm dialog leaves focus on the page body, not on "Review change".
- Measured after Esc and after "Go back", opened by keyboard and by mouse: document.activeElement is BODY each time.
- The next Tab starts again at the logo, so a keyboard user loses their place at the money step.
- SPEC section 13 says dialogs return focus on close.
- The "See the math" dialog on billing home does return focus to its button, so this is only the confirm dialog.
- Opening is right: focus lands on the heading and stays trapped inside.

Reproduce: as a paid owner open http://localhost:3300/billing/plan, add one seat, tab to "Review change", press Enter, then Esc. Script: docs/billing/.review/visual4/scripts/r4b.cjs.

Great looks like: after Esc, "Go back" or the X, focus is back on "Review change" with its ring showing. Add a browser test that checks the focused element after close.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/features/billing/plan-picker/change-confirm.tsx (Dialog onOpenChange and onClose, about lines 56 to 65) and its caller in plan-picker.tsx about line 807

blockers.title: Small polish gaps a top product would not ship
blockers.detail:
Fix in one sweep. Screenshots are in docs/billing/.review/visual4.

1. Invoices table at 768 px. The date wraps to two lines and the invoice number breaks in the middle: "TEST-" then "0001". The "For" text wraps too, while space sits unused before the PDF button. Keep the date, number and amount on one line each and let only "For" wrap. See sheets/_z15.png (http://localhost:3300/billing/invoices at 768, light and dark).

2. Setup guide on phones. On rows 4 and 5 the links "Pick a template" and "Pick a plan" start about 54 px to the right of the step title. The red "Open WMS" button on row 3 lines up with the title. Line the quiet links up the same way. Seen on the launcher and on Organization, both themes. See sheets/_s2.png.

3. Setup guide count on phones. The header says "2 of 5 done" and the row under it says "Show all steps (7 more)", or "(11 more)" with three apps. Five steps with eleven more reads as a mistake. Say what is hidden in the same terms as the header, such as "Show the other 4 steps", and keep the extra steps under their own line. See shots/s10-guide-open--phone-light.png and sheets/_n1.png.

4. Two select styles in one card. On Organization the role control in a member row is a plain browser select, with the default arrow and larger text on phones. The "Role" select in the invite form just below uses the design system select. Use the design system select in both. See sheets/_z5.png and sheets/_s1.png.

5. Two looks for the same test mode hint. Verify email shows a "TEST MODE" pill with "Open the email outbox to see your code." The code step on sign in shows a plain sentence: "Test mode: no real email is sent. Find the code in the dev outbox." Use the pill version on both. See sheets/_z8.png.
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing/invoices/page.tsx (table cells, lines 90 to 101); apps/portal/src/features/setup/setup-guide.tsx (phone row actions and the "Show all steps" label); apps/portal/src/app/(app)/settings/organization/member-rows.tsx (native select at lines 100 and 143); the code step of apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/login

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. 5 blockers (3 backend, 2 ui). The money flow itself held everywhere I pushed it: no fake charge, no double charge, no access without payment, every amount right to the cent. The blockers are at the edges: a person with no organization, a person in two organizations, an old session after a password reset, and a refresh on the new code sign in.

**How I tested**
- Drove the real product with Playwright and signed webhook calls on the shared dev stack: test gateway on, plan gate on (`ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0` in all six processes). Also the production build with no keys on port 3310.
- Made 8 new organizations and 7 invited people. Read `core.entitlements`, `billing_subscriptions`, `billing_invoices`, `billing_events`, `billing_emails` and the audit log after each step.
- No product code edited, no server restarted. Scripts, outputs and screenshots: `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/opqa4/`.

**Round 3 blockers, rechecked: all 7 of mine are fixed**
- Cancel with a bill open ends the plan today, voids the bill, charges nothing later, and says so on the page, the flash, the banner, the email and the activity line.
- Signed out links keep their path and query. `/billing?fix=payment` returns after sign in with "Update card" in focus.
- A retry after day 7 now mails "Your apps are view only now", and a plan the gateway closes says "We could not collect $164.00 after 5 tries".
- Removing an app that ends the bundle discount says so, with both prices, before confirm.
- App banners are right on the next request after pay, cancel, keep, pause and end.
- The billing only person lands on Billing, needs no code, and each app says "You have billing access only".
- An admin cannot make anyone a billing manager through the sign in API (403 on every variant I tried).

**What works, with real results**
- Wizard to signup: bad inputs, weak and guessable passwords, duplicate email, back, forward, refresh and a double click all hold. Signup to picker took 1.7 s.
- Trial: rows are source trial, 14 days out. Emails at 7, 3 and 1 days and at the end. Apps add and remove from lock screens. All four apps open in a trial and turn view only after it, with the write dialog.
- Checkout: declined, no funds and a failed bank step write no rows. Bank approval and TEST10 work; $355.68 matches on checkout, success, home and invoice.
- Changes: seats, warehouses, apps, monthly to yearly and back all match their invoices to the cent, including credit carried across changes. A declined change leaves every row as it was.
- Webhooks: replays answer "duplicate"; false, stale and cross organization events change no plan row; 6 bad signatures get 400.
- Failed payment: late, retries, last day email, view only, recovery by card in 2.5 s, plan closed by the gateway, paying again with no second trial.
- Cancel, keep, end, reactivate, pause, undo and start again all work. Yearly plans get no pause offer.
- Seats: invites hold a seat, guests and billing only do not, a canceled invite and a removed person free one, the floor follows.
- Roles: member and admin are refused on pages and on replayed server actions.
- WMS warehouse limit: price shown, added in the Portal, back in the WMS with the create form open.
- Production build with no keys: billing says it is off, money buttons are off, the test routes answer 404, and the browser console is clean.

**Smaller notes, not blockers**
- Dev pages log "preloaded but not used" warnings. The production build logs none.
- The billing job takes 2.5 to 5 s per run on dev, even with nothing to do.
- A locked account answers "That email and password do not match" for the right password. That is the security design, but it will confuse a real owner.

**Not verified**
- Real Stripe, real email, Google and Microsoft sign in.
- "Your bank needs to approve" at a renewal (the test gateway cannot reach it).
- Production with real keys.

**One thing I disturbed and put back**
- My sign in limit test locked the seeded owner `maya@northwind-robotics.example` for about 2 minutes. I cleared that one lock row in the local database and confirmed she signs in again (200). I also reset the passwords of four of my own test users.

blockers.title: The WMS reloads forever for a signed in person who has no organization
blockers.where: apps/wms/src/server/tenancy/lock-view.ts (loadLockView returns 'setup' when the person has no organization), apps/wms/src/app/locked/page.tsx (redirects 'setup' to /setup-warehouse), the WMS /setup-warehouse page (redirects back to /locked); CRM /welcome for the same person
blockers.detail:
Reproduce: make an account with no organization (POST /api/auth/sign-up/email only, or remove a member from their only organization). Open http://localhost:3000/ signed in.

What happens: the browser sits on /locked with a blank page and reloads it without end. I counted 61 page loads and 1,207 requests in 10 seconds. The tab cannot even be sent to another address while it runs. Script: docs/billing/.review/opqa4/105-noorg.js and 95-casey-wms.js.

Why: with no memberships loadLockView answers 'setup', /locked sends the person to /setup-warehouse, and that page sends a person with no WMS organization back to /locked (raw GET gives 307 /locked).

Who meets it: a member right after they are removed, a person whose workspace step failed, anyone who signs in to the WMS before they have an organization. Each such tab also hits the server about 6 times a second.

The four apps also disagree for this person. Portal, Projects and Pulse say "You are not in an organization yet. Create one in the Portal." The CRM runs its own 6 step wizard, makes an organization with one click on "Skip setup", says "Your workspace is ready", and then shows "CRM is not in your plan yet".

What great looks like: one answer in every app. A person with no organization sees one calm screen, "You are not in an organization yet", with one button to the Portal. No redirect between /locked and /setup-warehouse can loop. The CRM sends this person to the Portal too, so there is one front door. Add a test for a signed in person with zero memberships in each app.

blockers.title: Email links open the wrong organization for a person who is in two
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/links.ts and the email templates in packages/billing/src/emails (links carry no organization); apps/portal/src/server/orgs.ts resolveActiveOrg and listUserOrgs (a new session takes the first organization by name); the billing pages under apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing
blockers.detail:
Reproduce: Dana owns "R4QA Alpha" and is a member of "OPQA B". Signed out, open the link from her own failed payment email, http://localhost:3300/billing?fix=payment, and sign in.

What happens: she lands on Billing for OPQA B and reads "OPQA B has an active plan. Ask Sam Rivera to manage billing." Nothing says this is not the organization the email was about. The receipt link /billing/invoices/<her invoice> sends her to the same wrong page, with no message at all. "Pick a plan" from a trial email does the same. Script: docs/billing/.review/opqa4/87-twoorg-link.js.

Why: no link in any billing email names the organization. A new session has no active organization, so the Portal picks the first one by name, here the one where she is only a member. The same happens in a live session when the other organization is the active one.

Why it matters: the owner who gets "We could not charge your card" clicks the one button and is told to ask someone else. She has to guess that the switcher at the top is the fix, while the 7 days run.

What great looks like: every billing link carries the organization. The Portal switches to it when the person is a member, and then shows the page. If the person is not a member it says so in one line. A new session starts in the organization the person used last, or one they own, not the first by name. Add a browser test with one person in two organizations.

blockers.title: An old session can still cancel the plan for 5 minutes after a password reset
blockers.where: packages/auth/src/options.ts (cookieCache maxAge 5 minutes together with revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset); apps/portal/src/server/session.ts and apps/portal/src/server/billing/context.ts (billing reads and actions accept the cached session)
blockers.detail:
SPEC 5.5 says: after a reset, every old session is signed out.

Reproduce: sign in as an owner in browser one. In browser two run Forgot password, enter the code and save a new password. The session table now holds 1 row, the new one. Go back to browser one within 5 minutes.

What happens in browser one, the old session:
- /billing and /billing/cancel still open.
- The activity CSV still downloads (200).
- "Cancel my plan" works. The plan was set to end, with the audit line "Sam Rivera canceled the plan."
- At 2 minutes it still worked. At 5.3 minutes it was sent to sign in.
A session that had not been used for a while was signed out at once, so this hits exactly the sessions that are in use. Scripts: docs/billing/.review/opqa4/84-reset-fresh.js and 90-reset-write.js.

Why it matters: a password reset is what an owner does when they think someone else is in their account. For 5 more minutes that someone can still cancel the plan, change it or read the invoices.

What great looks like: after a reset the old session is refused on the very next request. At the least, every billing page and every billing action checks the session against the database (no cookie cache), as the WMS lock screen already does. Add a test: reset in one browser, then a billing action in the other is refused.

blockers.title: A refresh on the code sign in step throws the person back to an empty form
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(auth)/login (the "Email me a code instead" step keeps its state only in the browser page)
blockers.detail:
Reproduce: open /login, type the email, press "Email me a code instead". The screen says "Check your email". Now refresh, or go to another page and press Back.

What happens: the page is "Welcome back" again, with the email field empty. The code that was just mailed has no place to be typed. The person must type the email again and ask for a second code. Script: docs/billing/.review/opqa4/78-code.js.

Why it matters: this is the door for people without a password, and they leave the page to read their mail. On a phone the browser often reloads a tab when you come back from the mail app. The two sister screens already get this right: /verify-email and /reset-password keep the address in the link and survive a refresh.

What great looks like: the code step has its own address (for example /login?step=code with the email after the #, as /reset-password does). A refresh or Back shows the code field again with the same address and the same code still valid. Add a browser test: ask for a code, reload, enter the code, land on the page from `next`.

blockers.title: Small wrong turns on real paths
blockers.where: Plan banner for admins in CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse (planNoticeFor in packages/billing); apps/portal/src/app/(app)/billing/page.tsx (the "Dev override" badge); the invite seat offer in apps/portal settings/organization; PlanPicker in change mode; Portal /signup/company for a removed member; the Pulse seat note in PlanPicker
blockers.detail:
Each one is small. Together they are moments where a customer stops and wonders.

1. An admin cannot pay, but every app shows them "Your payment is late, so your apps are view only. Pay now to turn them back on." with the button "Update card". The button lands on Billing, which says only an owner or a billing manager can pay. Great: for a person who cannot pay, the banner names who can ("Ask Sam Rivera to update the card.") and has no pay button.

2. With the override switch on, the Portal shows a "DEV OVERRIDE" badge beside "TRIAL ENDED", says "Your apps are view only" and marks every app VIEW ONLY, while every app is in fact open. GO-LIVE keeps that switch on in production until step 11, and the roll back step turns it on again. Real customers would read staff words and a wrong state. Great: no staff words on a customer page, and no "view only" claim while the apps are open. Seen on the production build at port 3310.

3. The seat offer on an invite said "Add 1 seat for $32.80 more per month. You pay $1.09 today for the days left." The real sum was $24.05 for 22 days less $22.96 credit. The amount is right but the reason is not. Great: "You pay $1.09 today: $24.05 for the days left, less $22.96 credit."

4. On a paid plan, turning every app off in the picker leaves a dead button and "Pick at least one app." Great: one line that says "To stop paying for everything, cancel your plan" with the link.

5. A member who was just removed opens /billing and reads "Name your workspace. Good to meet you, Casey." as if they were new. The launcher says something else ("You are not in an organization yet"). Great: one screen for both, that says they are no longer in an organization and what they can do.

6. With Pulse and 6 seats the picker says: "The Pulse price is made for teams of up to 5 people. You picked 6 seats. All 6 people can use Pulse, at the price shown here. For a bigger team, talk to us." Three of the four sentences pull against each other. Great: one plain rule, as SPEC P8 has it.

blockers.title: "Email me a code instead" works once, then locks the person out: their password is deleted and no second code is ever mailed
blockers.detail:
Reproduced on the dev portal (port 3300) with /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec4/lockout.mjs. Real output: (1) sign up with a password, email code skipped: 200, core.account has one credential row. (2) First sign in by code works, email_verified becomes true, and core.account is now EMPTY. (3) Second time the screen says "a code is on its way", but no row reaches core.billing_emails after 15 seconds. (4) Sign in with the password chosen at signup: 401 Invalid email or password.

Why: Better Auth 1.7.21 `revokeUnprovenAccountAccess` deletes every core.account row and every session when an account whose email was never proven signs in with a code. That defense is right (my probe prehijack.mjs shows it stops a pre account hijack). But `maySignInWithCode` only mails a code to a person who still has a credential row with a password, and the first code sign in removes that row. So the second code is never sent while the screen says it was, and the password is gone with no word to the person.

Who it hits: every account that pressed "I will do this later" on the email code, every "no password" signup that skipped the code (their only way in is the code), and every older self signup account that was never asked to verify. "Forgot password" is the only way back and nothing says so. The e2e test in signin-code.spec.ts signs in by code only once per account, so it cannot see this.

Great looks like: a person who signed in by code can always do it again (second and tenth code arrive). If the old password is removed, one plain sentence says so and offers "Set a password". Add a browser test that signs in by code twice in a row for an account that never verified, and for a "no password" signup. Fixing blocker 2 with a real "switched off" flag untangles this, because "has no password row" then stops meaning two things.

blockers.title: A person who was switched off can switch themselves back on with "Forgot password" (auth review H3 undone)
blockers.detail:
Reproduced with /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec4/deactivated-reset.mjs. Real output: (2) credential row deleted the way WMS setUsersActive does it, sign in with the old password: 401. (3) POST /api/auth/email-otp/request-password-reset: 200 and a reset code is mailed. (4) POST /api/auth/email-otp/reset-password with that code: 200, and core.account has a new credential row. (5) Sign in with the new password: 200.

Why: docs/security/auth-review-2026-11-11.md H3 is binding context. A person is switched off by deleting their credential row, because their core.member row (often admin) stays; migrate-wms-identity.ts says "no credential row = no sign-in; reactivation goes through an admin password reset". The comment on `maySignInWithCode` knows the rule, but the reset by code path does not: the server actions and the raw endpoints mail a code to any address with a user row, and Better Auth `resetCredentialPassword` creates a credential row when none exists. origin/main had no self service reset at all (no sendResetPassword, no emailOTP), so this door is new on this branch. By reading the code, Google and Microsoft sign in open the same door (the provider links to the user row by email); not run, no client keys.

Impact: a person removed for cause who still reads their mailbox gets back into the Portal, CRM, Projects and Pulse with their old role in one minute.

Great looks like: being switched off is a fact the shared auth layer reads (a flag or table in core, checked inside createAuth on every instance), not "has no password row". No reset code, no sign in code and no social sign in works for a switched off person, at the server actions and at the raw /api/auth endpoints, with the same neutral answer as an unknown address. Tests: one unit test per door, plus a browser test that a switched off person gets no reset code and cannot reset.

blockers.title: An admin can take an owner's open billing invite and become a billing manager (no proof of the mailbox is needed to accept an invite)
blockers.detail:
Reproduced with /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec4/invite-takeover-admin.mjs. Real output: (1) owner invites a bookkeeper address with the billing role: 200. (2) A plain ADMIN calls /api/auth/organization/list-invitations (and get-full-organization): 200, sees the invitation id and role billing. (3) The admin signs up a new account with the invited address: 200 (signup needs no proof of the mailbox). (4) That account calls /api/auth/organization/accept-invitation: 200. core.member now holds the address with role `billing` and email_verified false. (5) /billing/team as that account: 200 and lists it as a billing manager.

Why: accepting an invite needs only the invitation id and a signed in account with the invited address. `requireEmailVerificationOnInvitation` is off, and the Portal's own /invite/<id> page with `joinInviteAction` makes the account and joins in one step with no proof (the proof only decides whether the email is marked verified). `billingAccessFor` gives canManage to the billing role, and cancel, pause, keep, retry payment, billing details and the card page do not ask for a verified email. So the admin can cancel or pause the plan and change billing details. SPEC P15: only an owner can add a billing manager, and admins cannot pay, change or cancel. This is the round 3 rule with one door left open. A plain member cannot do it (list answers 403), and Better Auth hides owner invites from admins, so the hole is the billing role.

Great looks like: an invite that gives the billing role can only be accepted by a person who proved the mailbox: the proof from the emailed link, or a verified email. Put it in `billingOrganizationOptions.beforeAcceptInvitation` so it holds at every app, and make `joinInviteAction` and `acceptInviteAction` say one plain sentence when refused. Better still, require a proven mailbox for every invite accept, since the Portal already marks the email verified when the link's proof checks out. Tests: an admin who signs up with the invited address is refused at the raw endpoint and in joinInviteAction, nothing is written; the real invited person with the emailed link still joins with no code.

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. Three backend blockers, each reproduced on the running dev portal with throwaway accounts that I removed afterwards (0 users, organizations, emails, codes and rate limit rows left). The round 3 blocker is fixed. Reviewed at commit 61081d9. No product code was edited and no shared server was restarted.

**The three blockers**
1. **Sign in by code works once, then locks the person out.** For an account that never verified its email, the first code sign in deletes the password row. After that no code is mailed, while the screen says one is on its way, and the old password answers 401.
2. **A switched off person can switch themselves back on.** "Forgot password" mails a code to an account whose credential row was deleted, and the reset makes a new one. This undoes H3 of the binding auth review. The door is new on this branch.
3. **An admin can take an owner's open billing invite.** The admin reads the invite id, signs up with the invited address (no proof of the mailbox is asked for) and accepts. The account then holds the billing role and can cancel or pause the plan.

**Round 3 blocker, rechecked: fixed**
- As a plain admin, at the Portal and at the CRM, every attempt answers 403 `BILLING_ROLE_OWNER_ONLY` and the database is unchanged:
  - giving the billing role to yourself (four spellings, plus a trailing slash on the path)
  - inviting an outsider with the billing role
  - taking the role from a bookkeeper, or removing them by id or by email
  - canceling the owner's open billing invite
- The owner can still invite a bookkeeper.

**What I ran**
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in `packages/billing`: 29 files, 537 tests pass with the database up.
- Seven probe scripts against the dev portal (3300), the CRM (3100) and the production mode portal with no keys (3310).
- I did not rerun the Playwright suite or a build. Nobody has run real Stripe. The Google and Microsoft part of blocker 2 is from reading the code, not from a run.

**Checked and sound**
- **Webhooks:** the signature is checked on the raw body first, and the ledger row and the state change commit together. An unsigned test webhook answers 400.
- **Production with no keys:** test gateway pages 404, `/dev/outbox` 404, test webhook 404, Stripe webhook 503, job tick 503.
- **Money:** no price or amount comes from the browser. I checked the catalog cents by hand; yearly and bundle amounts are whole cents.
- **Organization scope:** invoices, PDFs and the activity export only read the session's organization.
- **Redirects:** the helpers take same origin paths only.
- **Pre account hijack by code sign in:** closed. The first person's password and sessions are removed.
- **Invite ids:** a plain member cannot list invites.
- **Migrations 0007 to 0010:** additive and safe to run again.
- **Secrets:** no key shaped string in the tree.

**Not blockers, worth fixing**
1. Real Stripe is still unrun. This is the largest open risk.
2. Anyone can use up another address's code budget. The send limits (5 per 10 minutes, 20 per day) count anonymous requests, and one budget covers verify, reset and sign in codes. Twenty requests a day block a chosen person's reset and code sign in.
3. A 6 digit code allows about 100 guesses a day per address. Consider a longer code or a lock.
4. Outside Vercel, a made up single `x-forwarded-for` value gives a caller their own rate limit bucket. Set `TRUST_PROXY` on any other host.
5. Database tests still skip silently when Postgres is down.
6. Cancel, pause and undo write the plan row without the organization lock that webhooks take.
7. A first payment that Stripe leaves `incomplete` and then expires would be stored as an ended plan, and could mail "Your plan has ended" for a plan that never started. Check this against real Stripe.
8. With WMS and Pulse and no per user app, the Pulse limit of 5 seats caps the whole organization.

Round 3 blockers: 9 of 10 are closed, most better than asked.
- "Email me a code instead" works on signup and login: 3 fields, no password, no inbox trip, 0.8 s to sign in after the code.
